title: Stratified perfect description of the integral completed category
statement: Use the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and schemes of [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here noetherian means that $T$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, finite-dimensional means a finite bound on the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets, and invertible means that $\ell\cdot1$ is a unit in each local ring. Put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $K$ belongs to [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], including its compatible etale-origin witnesses; (ii) there is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] such that on each stratum $K$ is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_T\otimes_A^L P$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$, meaning a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules; (iii) $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf, after a finite stratification, is pro-etale locally $A_T\otimes_A N$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $N$. These conditions also describe exactly the category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] whenever that notation is used over such a $T$, with the same completed ring sheaf and reduction functors. This full subcategory is closed under shifts, cones, standard truncations and cohomology sheaves placed in degree zero.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1; Proposition 6.6.11; Proposition 6.8.11(1),(3). Adapted to the explicitly retained compatible etale-origin witnesses and uniform reduction bounds of the DAG; those clauses must be verified, not identified by notation.

proof.text: The ring $A$ is adically complete. Compatible representatives $x_n$ satisfy $|x_m-x_n|_E\le|\varpi|_E^n$ for $m\ge n$. Completeness of $E$ gives a limit in the closed unit ball $A$, lying in every closed residue ball $x_n+\varpi^nA$. The intersection $\bigcap_n\varpi^nA=0$ gives uniqueness.

Use the restriction-unit lemma throughout. Each term of a completed perfect constant is the inverse limit of its finite-projective torsion reductions (commute finite sums and the defining idempotent with limits). Torsion-limit completeness, scalar restriction and the constant-completion equivalence (local equals Koszul completeness) make the bounded complex complete. Finite-stratum detection gives completeness for (ii); the uniform-model lemma supplies boundedness and uniformly constructible reductions.

For (i), the uniform reduction criterion gives bounded constructible residue. Take its etale origin, then the finite-field model lemma gives a residue-perfect stratification. Restrictions are complete by the restriction-unit lemma; step 1 verifies coefficient completeness. Each stratum is Noetherian: locally closed in a Noetherian affine open, and quasi-compact since $|T|$ is Noetherian. Apply residue-lisse perfect lifting on each stratum to obtain (ii).

Conversely (ii) has complete underlying object and a uniform constructible reduction profile by step 2. The uniform reduction criterion supplies the common tower models and compatible etale-origin witnesses. These are precisely all clauses of (i).

For (ii) implies (iii), exact constant realization and flatness give $\mathcal H^q(B_U\otimes_A P)=B_U\otimes_A H^q(P)$. Kernels in finite-projective terms are finite over the Noetherian DVR, so their quotient cohomology is finite and finitely presented. Step 2 supplies boundedness.

For a finitely presented $A$-module $N$, the kernel of $A^r\twoheadrightarrow N$ is finite and torsion-free, hence finite free. Its two-term resolution realizes $B_U\otimes_A N$ by a perfect complex. Thus each sheaf in (iii), in degree zero, satisfies (ii) and (i). Finite Postnikov devissage and triangulated closure now give (i) for $K$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), finite resolutions and Postnikov devissage

proof.text: With the stipulated identical coefficient and reduction functors, both constructibility definitions give the same finite-stratum condition. The uniform reduction criterion identifies their uniform reduction requirements. Intrinsic completeness gives the detailed Roos triangle by constant-completion comparison. Conversely that triangle identifies $K$ with the quotient completion object, which is intrinsically complete by the Koszul reflector. This proves the detailed-category assertion.

Shifts and cones follow from triangulated closure. Good truncations retain the original cohomology sheaves in the retained degrees and give zero elsewhere; hence they still satisfy (iii). A cohomology sheaf in degree zero does also, since zero has the model $N=0$. Apply the equivalences just proved.

proof_origin.place: Propositions 6.6.11 and 6.8.11(3), with explicit DAG uniform-tower/witness and coefficient comparisons; truncation closure proved directly from the existing characterization
